content.text:
Here are three papers on evaluating RAG systems. The search results were thin, so I haven't checked publication dates or venues beyond what the snippets showed.

1. **LIT-RAGBench: Benchmarking Generator Capabilities of Large Language Models in Retrieval-Augmented Generation** (LREC 2026). It tests the generator side of RAG: integrating evidence from long contexts, multi-step reasoning, table interpretation, and abstaining when the evidence is missing. It appears on the ACL Anthology, not arXiv. [Link](https://preview.aclanthology.org/ingest-lrec/2026.lrec-main.427/)

2. **MTRAGEval / SemEval-2026 Task 8** (Athanasiou et al., reportedly March 2026). It is a multi-turn RAG benchmark covering passage retrieval, grounded response generation, and end-to-end RAG. A secondary summary is my only source for the attribution and date. I couldn't confirm an arXiv listing. [Link](https://api.emergentmind.com/topics/mtrageval)

3. **Benchmarking Large Language Models in Retrieval-Augmented Generation** (the RGB benchmark, 2023). It is older, but it is the foundational work that newer benchmarks build on. It tests four abilities: noise robustness, negative rejection, information integration, and counterfactual robustness. [Link](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2309.01431)

The search also surfaced *Evaluation of Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Survey*. It proposes a unified evaluation process that separates retrieval and generation metrics and adds requirements like latency and robustness. I didn't find its date or venue. [Link](https://themoonlight.io/review/evaluation-of-retrieval-augmented-generation-a-survey)

If you need arXiv papers from 2026 specifically, I can run a more targeted search.
